issues.description: Field: Animal.name. The UML diagram in problem_statement.md declares the Animal.name attribute as type String (problem_statement.md line 27). The textual instructions in the same problem statement explicitly instruct students to use StringBuilder for the name attribute (problem_statement.md line 85). The provided reference implementation in the solution repository declares the field as private String name in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java (solution). This inconsistent specification (String vs StringBuilder) will confuse students about the expected field type, the getter/setter signatures, and how to assemble messages that use the name. It can lead students to implement a StringBuilder-based API that does not match the reference solution and tests, or conversely to follow the solution while contradicting the textual guidance.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the intended type for Animal.name consistent across all artifacts. Choose one of the two options and apply it everywhere (problem statement UML, textual instructions, template code, and reference solution/tests):

Option A (recommended for minimal change): standardize on String. Update problem_statement.md to remove the StringBuilder requirement (edit the textual instruction at line 85) and, if present, update the UML to keep name: String. Keep the reference solution's private String name and its getName()/setName(String) methods. Update any example code in the statement or templates to use String.

Option B (if you prefer StringBuilder): update the UML to name: StringBuilder (problem_statement.md line 27), and update the reference solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) and the template to declare private StringBuilder name, provide a constructor and getter/setter consistent with StringBuilder semantics (e.g., getName(): StringBuilder or getNameAsString(): String), and update all call sites (other classes and tests) to use toString() where a String is required. Ensure the problem statement examples and instructions clearly state the chosen API.

Apply the chosen change to the test harness and sample/template code so students and automated tests expect the same field type and accessor signatures.
